correctness.rationale: For a one-dimensional graph the descending link is a discrete set of earlier neighbors, so exactly one earlier neighbor is equivalent to descending domination. The universal case analysis on the hub and each leaf pair produces an exact simplicial join-plus-cones equality, with reverse realizations of all generators. The main join has the homotopy type of \(3^m\) top-dimensional spheres, each of \(2m\) additional cones attaches along a sphere already bounding a cone in the main join, adding one top sphere; \(m=1\) is checked separately. The same decomposition proves the complete f-vector. Full-face enumeration for all \((2m+1)!\) orders with \(m=1,2,3,4\) and original mod-two boundary ranks corroborate but are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete infinite-family classification of full strong matching complexes for the connected Dutch-windmill triangle family, rather than an isolated numerical small case. The one-point gluing of triangles creates a join of four-choice blocks and \(2m\) null-attaching suspension spheres, producing an exact exponentially growing top Betti number \(3^m+2m\). It exhibits a substantive difference from the previously calculated contractible ordinary edge-matching complex on the very same graph and extends beyond the known path/cycle/star strong-Morse cases. Neither the join-plus-cones mechanism nor the full f-vector is a routine restatement of those earlier results.
